```{r, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
has_quanteda <- requireNamespace("quanteda", quietly = TRUE) &&
  utils::packageVersion("quanteda") >= "4.5.0" &&
  isTRUE(l10n_info()[["UTF-8"]])
```

A teacher may want to choose clear, contrasting examples, ask learners to
explain patterns, and reuse the activity in another class. This guide prepares
**a learner handout and a separate teacher record from explicitly reviewed
source occurrences**. Learners need a browser or a printed handout, not R.
An R user prepares the search and runs the input/output steps; a teacher can
edit the selection and activity tables.

Use development **ldfreq 0.5.0.9001**; see the
[installation instructions](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/index.html#install).
`ddl_material()` and `ddl_material_write()` are installed examples to source
explicitly, not exported functions. Construction revalidates the existing
phrase review and requires optional **quanteda >= 4.5.0**. Japanese input also
requires a UTF-8 `LC_CTYPE` locale; the bilingual demo runs in that environment.
Reopening a completed
material record and writing it again uses only ldfreq's required packages.

## Run the authored English and Japanese examples

```{r ddl-demo, eval=has_quanteda}
demo <- new.env(parent = globalenv())
sys.source(system.file("examples", "ddl-materials-demo.R",
  package = "ldfreq", mustWork = TRUE), demo)
helper <- demo$helper
x <- demo$materials$en # Use $ja for the Japanese handout.
x$selected[c("phrase_id", "pre", "keyword", "post", "citation")]
x$candidate_summary
```

The English examples contrast uses of *take off*. The Japanese examples
contrast contextual interpretations of *ashi o hippatta*. They are authored,
MIT-licensed illustrations with manually specified token boundaries, not
observations from a textbook corpus or an evaluation of an automatic analyzer.
The new teaching-selection criterion is separate from the earlier phrase-sense
review. Both clear interpretations can be selected for comparison.

Each handout contains two selected examples. Other accepted, unresolved and
unreviewed candidates remain in the private record. Selecting examples does
not imply that the complete candidate collection has been reviewed.

```{r ddl-write, eval=has_quanteda}
output <- tempfile("ldfreq-teaching-")
files <- helper$ddl_material_write(x, output)
stopifnot(identical(readRDS(files["record"]), x))
basename(files)
```

For actual teaching, replace the temporary directory with a lasting **new**
directory inside an existing parent, for example `"materials/lesson-01"`.
An existing directory or file is rejected; the writer never overwrites it.
Open `learner.html` in a browser and print using the paper size you need.
Check the print preview at the intended size, especially for long contexts
or citations. Browser fonts and pagination can differ.

| File | Audience and contents |
| --- | --- |
| `learner.html` | Selected original KWIC contexts, bold matched expressions, teacher-written prompts, response space, citations and usage notices. Self-contained UTF-8 HTML with print styling; no scripts or external assets. |
| `teacher.csv` | The same selected occurrences in display order, original segment text, IDs, source coordinates, decisions, prompts and teacher notes. UTF-8; import fields as literal text. |
| `material.rds` | Complete private record: original search and text, all decisions including pending ones, selection, activities, source declarations, settings and session. Keep it for reuse; do not distribute it as the learner handout. |

Teacher notes, decision reasons, unselected rows and complete source records
are not embedded in the learner file, including hidden elements. The selected
KWIC still includes its original surrounding text: inspect that context before
distribution. A selected context can contain another expression that is also
matched elsewhere in the review.

## Prepare your own reviewed candidates

Start with the [phrase-review workflow](annotated-corpora.html#review-phrase-matches).
It accepts complete source-aligned annotations and an explicitly declared
phrase list. Its existing search matches **at least two tokens**, exactly and
case-sensitively, by their original surface forms. A word such as *influence*
alone is outside this first recipe; an explicitly tokenized sequence can be
searched. Japanese inflections and spelling variants are not automatically
merged. Keep the analyzer, dictionary, token unit and original text in the
annotation record; see [Japanese annotations](japanese-annotations.html).

Use a criterion such as "clear contrasting contexts for this observation task".
An example rejected for this activity is not thereby incorrect language.
The following continues from `before`, a `phrase_list_review()` result:

```{r ddl-decisions, eval=FALSE}
write.csv(before$worksheet, "decisions.csv", row.names = FALSE,
  na = "<MISSING>", fileEncoding = "UTF-8")
# In the table, edit only status, reviewer and reason; keep every original row.
decisions <- read.csv("decisions.csv", colClasses = "character",
  check.names = FALSE, na.strings = "<MISSING>", encoding = "UTF-8")
review <- helper$phrase_list_review(before$source, before$criterion, decisions)
```

Use `accepted`, `rejected`, `unresolved` or `unreviewed` as documented in that
workflow. Only accepted IDs can be selected for a handout. You need not finish
reviewing every candidate, but pending candidates remain pending in the saved
record. A no-match target remains in the review's count table. A handout needs
at least one selected example; no matches or no accepted examples produce an
input error rather than an empty worksheet presented as a completed lesson.

## Supply the teaching tables

```{r ddl-tables, eval=has_quanteda}
x$activities
x$items
x$sources
```

| Table | Required columns and interpretation |
| --- | --- |
| `activities` | Unique `activity_id`, learner-facing `prompt`, private `teacher_note` (use `""` if empty). Rows set activity order. |
| `items` | Unique accepted `occurrence_id` and its `activity_id`. Row order sets example order within each activity. Every activity must have an example; accepted examples not listed here are not distributed. |
| `sources` | `document_id`, `segment_id`, learner-facing `citation` and `usage`. Supply exactly one row for each selected source pair, with nonblank attribution and usage text. |

IDs and text columns must be character vectors without missing values. These
tables can be stored as UTF-8 CSV and read with `colClasses = "character"`.
The activity prompt can contain several numbered questions separated by
newlines. Teacher notes can describe the intended contrast, alternative
interpretations or discussion points; they are not automatically correct
answers. The source `usage` text is a declaration supplied by the teacher,
not an automated license check or permission grant.

```{r ddl-build, eval=has_quanteda}
rebuilt <- helper$ddl_material(
  review = x$review,
  activities = x$activities,
  items = x$items,
  sources = x$sources,
  title = x$title,
  language = "en" # "ja" changes the fixed handout labels.
)
stopifnot(identical(rebuilt$selected, x$selected))
```

Every input string is treated as literal text, not HTML or Markdown.
Emphasis is applied only to the original matched span. No source text is
rewritten, normalized or silently shortened. Formula-like character fields
in the teacher CSV receive an apostrophe prefix for display; the unmodified
values remain in the RDS. This CSV is an output reference, not the editable
review worksheet.

Different phrase IDs at the same or nested source spans remain different
candidates. Choose which ones to distribute; the recipe does not silently
deduplicate them or convert their selected proportions into corpus frequencies.
The material fingerprint detects accidental changes; it does not establish
that annotation, attribution, permissions or pedagogical judgments are correct.

## Design the observation task

The authored prompts ask learners to compare contexts, group interpretations,
explain their evidence, check another example, and produce their own use.
The teacher supplies the further example and decides how to discuss competing
explanations. Neither highlighting an expression nor deleting a word by itself
establishes an effective data-driven learning activity.

Use the [textbook progression guide](textbook-progression.html) to inspect where
target expressions recur and choose revision opportunities. That concordance
record and the phrase-review record have different input formats and IDs;
they are not interchangeable. A general corpus, a local textbook and a selected
classroom worksheet also represent different collections. Retain their source
and selection boundaries instead of treating the handout as a representative
frequency sample.

This recipe does not download corpora, parse textbook PDFs, infer teaching
level, generate readings or furigana, choose examples by a quality score,
collect learner responses or grade them. Such information, when needed, must
come from an explicit source or teacher judgment.

## Reopen and reproduce without a new search

```{r ddl-reopen, eval=FALSE}
library(ldfreq)
helper <- new.env(parent = globalenv())
sys.source(system.file("examples", "ddl-materials.R",
  package = "ldfreq", mustWork = TRUE), helper)
saved <- readRDS("materials/lesson-01/material.rds")
helper$ddl_material_write(saved, "materials/lesson-01-copy")
```

This uses the stored examples and original session record without loading
quanteda or searching again. To change the selection or prompts, rebuild with
`ddl_material()` from the saved review and revised teaching tables. Do not edit
the sealed record or its fingerprint to bypass the source checks.
